works.title: Vertically aligned dual-channel metal-organic framework nanosheet membranes for gas separation
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Pulp and Paper Engineering
State Key Laboratory of Materials-Oriented Chemical Engineering
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
works.abstract: The nanostructure of two-dimensional (2D) membranes is crucial for their separation performance. However, in conventional 2D membranes, guest species unavoidably permeate through tortuous pathways, resulting in effective transport lengths that are orders of magnitude greater than the membrane thickness. Here, we propose vertically aligned metal-organic framework (MOF) nanosheet membranes featuring bimodal porosity: intrinsic lateral pores within the MOF nanosheets and interlamellar pores between them, forming an ultralow-tortuosity, dual-sieving channel system for efficient gas separation. Despite their relatively large thickness, the resulting MOF nanosheet membranes exhibit a high H 2 permeance of 16673 GPU (up to an order of magnitude higher than the reported average) along with an H 2 /CO 2 separation selectivity of 325 under standardized atmospheric Wicke-Kallenbach conditions (zero transmembrane partial pressure difference). This work not only provides a promising membrane platform for H 2 /CO 2 separation but also offers an alternative strategy for constructing next-generation molecular sieve membranes.

works.title: Revisiting the Characteristics and Performance of Acid-Treated Polyamide Membranes: Fundamental Insights and Implications
institutions: Shenzhen General Institute of Architectural Design and Research (China)
Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
The University of Hong Kong , , Pokfulam , ,
Shenzhen Machinery Institute Architectural Design Co Ltd , ,
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology , , ,
Tsinghua University, Shenzhen International Graduate School , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract Acid treatment of polyamide reverse osmosis (RO) and nanofiltration (NF) membranes is a commonly used approach for membrane cleaning and modification. However, there are contradictory observations on the effects of acid treatment in the current literature. Herein, we systematically characterized the changes in the physicochemical properties of both RO and NF membranes under different acid treatment conditions. Both acid-treated RO and NF membranes exhibited similar surface physicochemical characteristics compared with their respective original membranes. Interestingly, the acid-treated RO membrane showed a nearly doubled water permeance while maintaining high salt rejection. During the acid treatment, the fully aromatic RO membrane underwent selective removal of monomers/oligomers from the bottom region of its asymmetric polyamide layer, as evidenced by the appearance of N-rich molecules in the acid rinsing solution and the increased O/N ratio of the polyamide bottom side. At the same time, the O/N ratio of the polyamide top surface was not affected. In comparison, no release of monomers/oligomers was detected during the acid treatment of the semiaromatic NF membrane. Correspondingly, the NF membrane had a comparable water permeance before and after acid treatment. In the current study, the acid-treated RO membrane demonstrated improved water permeance and stable rejection of NaCl and several micropollutants, suggesting that acid treatment could be used as a polishing strategy to improve the performance of RO membranes for high-efficiency water treatment.

works.title: Adsorptive Membranes for PFAS Removal: Current Status, Design Principles, and Research Needs
works.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are contaminants of concern due to their persistence, occurrence in natural waters, and association with adverse health outcomes. Producing potable water from PFAS-impacted sources requires selectively removing PFAS from complex waters. Adsorptive membranes are an emerging strategy for PFAS removal due to their tunable architectures and chemistries, modularity, and high water permeances. However, it is difficult to compare adsorptive membrane performance across studies and identify membrane properties governing PFAS removal due to the diversity of materials, architectures, testing conditions, and reported performance metrics. This review critically evaluates the state of PFAS adsorptive membranes by examining nanofiber membranes, asymmetric membranes, adsorptive nanofiltration (NF) membranes, and ion exchange membranes used for adsorptive PFAS removal. We highlight structure-property-performance relationships, assess current testing strategies, and recommend standard performance metrics to enable cross-study comparisons. We further compare adsorptive membrane performance to conventional reverse osmosis (RO) and NF membranes. Finally, we apply the convection-diffusion-adsorption (CDA) model to published PFAS breakthrough data to gain mechanistic insights into the role of membrane properties and operating parameters on PFAS removal. Overall, this review provides a framework for evaluating adsorptive membranes, identifies key research gaps, and establishes design criteria to advance adsorptive PFAS separations.

works.title: Cyclic dipeptide reaction-induced in situ self-assembly interfacial polymerization for high-flux organic solvent nanofiltration polyamide membranes
works.abstract: Rapid, disordered network formation during interfacial polymerization (IP) broadens the pore-size distribution of polyamide organic solvent nanofiltration membranes, limiting both permeance and sieving precision. Here, we developed a reaction-induced self-assembly strategy using diamino cyclic dipeptide monomers and trimesoyl chloride (TMC). Amidation is proposed to increase the amphiphilicity of nascent oligomers, while intermolecular hydrogen bonding promotes local organization and suppresses disordered network formation. Model reactions, transmission electron microscopy, and grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering supported reaction-induced short-range ordering. The optimized LL-TMC membrane exhibited a narrow pore-size distribution centered at 0.82 nm and a methanol permeance of 40.8 ± 1.4 L·bar−1·h−1·m−2. It sharply distinguished Congo red (697 Da) from Solvent Red 43 (648 Da), with rejections of 95.3 ± 1.5% and 24.5 ± 6.1%, respectively, and separated both dyes in a mixed-solute system. This study indicates that regulating the local structural evolution during IP through monomer molecular design is a feasible approach to optimizing the pore size distribution of polyamide membranes and achieving synergistic enhancement of high permeance and high sieving precision.

works.title: Climbing the green ladder - toward a greener synthesis of polymers of intrinsic microporosity for separation membranes
works.abstract: Polymer membranes are materials that have a broad applicability for gas or liquid separation. Among them the polymers of intrinsic microporosity (PIMs) and especially PIM-1 are a promising material class. Its conventional synthesis relies on base-catalyzed polycondensation conducted in petrochemical solvents, raising concerns regarding toxicity, sustainability and environmental impact. To address these limitations, we systematically evaluated the synthesis of the polymer in a wide range of greener solvent systems in combination with both the typical fluor-containing PIM-1 comonomer along with the less hazardous, chlorine-containing comonomer. Through comprehensive solvent screening and optimization of reaction conditions, a greener reaction protocol that yields PIM-1 with molecular characteristics comparable to those produced via the standard process in dimethylformamide was established. Subsequent gas-separation and organic solvent nanofiltration testing of the resulting membrane, performed on both dense films and thin-film composite membranes, demonstrated permeation and selectivity values fully comparable to those of PIM-1 synthesized via the classical route. This study highlights that greener solvents and less toxic monomers can effectively replace conventional reagents without compromising polymer quality or membrane performance, thereby providing a viable, greener pathway for producing high-performance PIM materials.

works.title: Ciśnieniowe procesy membranowe w gospodarce wodno-ściekowej przemysłu galwanicznego
works.abstract: A review, with 39 refs. published in 2005–2025, focusing on heavy metal removal efficiency, membrane properties, process operating conditions, membrane fouling phenomena, and energy consumption. The microfiltration (MF) and ultrafiltration (UF) processes, used as preliminary treatment stages for electroplating wastewater, were discussed. However, they require the use of additional chemical substances. Techniques such as micellar-enhanced microfiltration (MEMF), micellarenhanced ultrafiltration (MEUF), and polymer-enhanced ultrafiltration (PEUF) were presented; which enable heavy metal rejection rate of approx. 89–99%. Furthermore, nanofiltration (NF) and reverse osmosis (RO) processes were compared; these allow for the direct removal of various heavy metals with efficiencies of 74–99% and 94.2–99.9%, resp. However, the application of RO is limited by high operating pressures and costs, higher energy consumption, and membrane susceptibility to fouling. Therefore, integrated membrane systems, such as UF/NF or UF/ RO, appear to be particularly promising. Their application can not only reduce the environmental pollution load but also enable the recovery of heavy metals from the retentate and their subsequent reuse in electroplating processes.

works.title: Desalinated wastewater for aquaponic reuse: challenge and impact
institutions: National Institute of Applied Science and Technology
works.abstract: This study looked into whether it’s possible and safe to use treated and desalinated municipal wastewater in a pilot aquaponics system. This system combined Nile tilapia fish with three growing. Deep-water culture (DWC), nutrient film technique (NFT), and grow beds. The wastewater went through several stages: an aerated moving bed biofilm reactor, a constructed wetland, sand and activated-carbon filters, and finally nanofiltration-reverse osmosis. This treatment removed 44% of COD, 95.6% of ammonia, and 33% of phosphate. The nanofiltration step removed about two-thirds of bivalent dissolved salts, 57% of sodium, 45% of chloride, and 39% of nitrates. Some micropollutants were removed, by 66%. During the experiment, the aquaponic water had an electrical coductivity between 0.5 and 2.2 mS/cm, a pH from 6.0 to 8.3, and a temperature ranging from 14 to 29 °C. All the fish survived, and their average daily weight gain was 1.97 g/day in Tank 1 and 0.86 and 1.26 g/day in Tank 2. The DWC, NFT, and grow beds successfully grew lettuce, cauliflower, endive, mint, basil, strawberry, tomato, fennel, and pepper. Tests found no Salmonella in the water, fish, or crops. However, some substances were still present in the DWC water, including benzotriazole (32.7 ng/L), carbamazepine (68.9 ng/L), and metoprolol (12 ng/L). The plants had nitrogen content between 0.18% and 0.41%, and their levels of phenol, sugar, proline, and phosphorus indicated good nutritional quality. In summary, using membrane-based treatment allowed the reuse of wastewater for aquaponics. However, it’s important to keep monitoring for nutrient imbalances and any leftover micropollutants.

works.title: Waste-Derived Zwitterionic Bacterial Cellulose Membranes with Enhanced Silica and Scaling Control for Sustainable Nanofiltration Pretreatment
institutions: Khalifa University of Science and Technology
Khalifa University of Science and Technology , , , P.O. Box 127788,
works.abstract: Abstract Bacterial cellulose (BC) membranes were engineered via kombucha fermentation with the incorporation of polyethylene glycol (PEG-600 and PEG-1000, 1–2%, w/v) to tailor pore formation and enhance structural stability. Subsequently, the BC membrane was functionalized with chitosan polyampholyte (CPA) to introduce zwitterionic properties for fouling mitigation. The incorporation of 2% PEG-1000 enhances BC production and mechanical properties, with elongation increasing from 20.3% to 49.7%. The zwitterionic modification leads to reduced pore size and altered surface morphology of BC membrane. The zwitterionic CPA-BC membrane exhibits effective pretreatment performance, achieving accumulated removals of 45% for soluble silica, 35% for calcium (Ca2+), and 19% for sulfate (SO42–), while maintaining a stable flux of 20 L m–2 h–1 over 17 h. CPA-BC pretreatment mitigates surface fouling of the commercial nanofiltration (NF) membrane, as evidenced by optical coherence tomography (OCT) and digital image processing, which reveal reduced surface coverage from 99.4% to 64.8%. This contributes to reducing the rapid flux decline observed with pretreatment, from 42 L m–2 h–1 at 2 h to 29 L m–2 h–1 at 17 h, compared to a rapid decline to 7 L m–2 h–1 within 2 h without pretreatment. The findings demonstrate the technical potential of waste-derived zwitterionic BC membranes to offer an effective and sustainable pretreatment strategy for controlling silica fouling and scaling, enabling improved stability and performance of desalination systems.

works.title: Heat stable salts in amine-based gas treatment: Formation mechanisms, impacts, reclamation, and hybrid mitigation strategies
works.abstract: Heat stable salts (HSS) are persistent, non-regenerable salts formed when protonated amines associate with acid anions that are not removed under normal regeneration conditions. Their accumulation reduces the fraction of active amine and may impair acid-gas absorption, while their effects on corrosion and foaming depend on anion identity, solvent formulation, co-contaminants, and operating conditions. This review critically examines HSS formation mechanisms, physicochemical characteristics, analytical determination, operational impacts, and conventional and emerging reclamation technologies. Solution purging, neutralization, thermal reclamation, and ion exchange are compared with electrodialysis, bipolar membrane electrodialysis, adsorption, electrosorption, electromagnetic separation, nanofiltration, and hybrid processes in terms of removal performance, amine retention, chemical and energy requirements, regeneration, fouling, waste generation, and industrial readiness. Ion exchange remains one of the most established options for deep HSS removal, with reported efficiencies of 77–97%; however, resin capacity loss, regenerant demand, and spent-regenerant management remain important constraints. Membrane-based technologies offer potential for selective removal and reduced chemical consumption, but their performance depends on anion-specific transport and rejection, amine concentration, operating conditions, and membrane properties. To address the need for process integration, an ion-exchange/anion-adsorptive-membrane side-stream configuration is proposed for lean-amine purification. This conceptual design aims to combine primary HSS removal with membrane polishing while limiting amine loss. Laboratory- and pilot-scale validation, together with techno-economic assessment, is required to establish its performance and industrial feasibility.

works.title: Carbon Nanomembranes as Precision Platforms for Subnanometer Molecular and Ionic Transport
institutions: Southern Marine Science and Engineering Guangdong Laboratory (Guangzhou)
Department of Chemical Engineering, Hebei Petroleum University of Technology, Chengde 067000, China
Faculty of Physics, Bielefeld University, 33615 Bielefeld, Germany
Guangdong Basic Research Center of Excellence for Ecological Security and Green Development, Southern Marine Science and Engineering Guangdong Laboratory (Guangzhou), Guangzhou 511458, China
works.abstract: Carbon nanomembranes (CNMs) are an emerging class of ultrathin carbon sheets with intrinsic sub–nanometer porosity and chemically programmable interfaces. Unlike other two–dimensional (2D) membranes, CNMs uniquely combine molecular–scale thickness, high pore density, and large–area scalability, enabling a transport regime that approaches the selectivity and efficiency of biological channels while retaining the robustness of synthetic materials. In this perspective, we argue that CNMs constitute a versatile platform for precision transport of water, gases, and ions. We first introduce a structural design toolkit that links precursor chemistry, cross–linking conditions, and support architecture to tunable parameters such as thickness. We then discuss the underlying transport physics in sub–nanometer CNM channels, highlighting single–file water permeation, adsorption–diffusion–controlled transport, and hydration–shell–mediated ion sieving. On this basis, we revisit CNM applications, ultrafast water permeation, gas sieving, and ion discrimination, not as isolated case studies, but as demonstrations of a unified design principle: controlling molecular structure and interfacial chemistry at the angstrom scale to engineer function. Finally, we outline key challenges and opportunities, including defect management, scalable fabrication, and integration into device architectures. By combining sub–nanometer confinement, molecular–scale thickness, and tunable interfacial chemistry, CNMs offer a synthetic platform for exploring transport principles relevant to biological channels and developing membrane devices for separation and energy storage.

works.title: Wettability-tailored recycled pet nanofibrous membranes for efficient oil/water emulsion separation
works.abstract: In this study, recycled polyethylene terephthalate was electrospun into nanofibrous membranes and surface-modified to develop super-hydrophilic and super-hydrophobic membranes for oil/water emulsion separation. To this end, two chemical modification strategies were employed: a sol–gel method based on tetraethyl orthosilicate to impart super-hydrophilicity, and they used of methyltrichlorosilane to induce super-hydrophobicity. FTIR and EDS analyses provided complementary evidence of silicon- and oxygen-containing species associated with the modified membrane surfaces. FESEM analysis revealed distinct surface morphologies after modification, including silica-associated surface structures in the super-hydrophilic membrane and hierarchical roughness in the super-hydrophobic membrane. Contact angle measurements showed that the pristine PET nanofibers were relatively hydrophobic, with a water contact angle of about 87° ± 1.12; after surface modification, the super-hydrophilic membrane showed a near-zero contact angle, while the super-hydrophobic membrane reached approximately 162° ± 2.8. Additionally, the team measured the underwater oil contact angle for the super-hydrophilic membrane at approximately 165–167°± 3.3, demonstrating its strong oil repellency in aqueous environments. Filtration tests showed that the super-hydrophilic membrane exhibited higher water flux, consistent with its enhanced surface hydrophilicity, whereas the superhydrophobic membrane showed lower water permeability. Mechanical tests further revealed that surface modification improved tensile strength; notably, the super-hydrophobic membrane exhibited a higher Young’s modulus due to the formation of stiffer surface layers. Ultimately, this study demonstrated that targeted surface modification of recycled PET nanofibers can significantly enhance wettability properties, filtration performance, and water/oil separation efficiency, leading to high-value recycled membranes suitable for environmental and industrial applications. Moreover, Both the super-hydrophilic and super-hydrophobic membranes achieved an oil/water separation efficiency of approximately 97 ± 2.4%.

works.title: Coupled Dynamic Modeling of a Brackish-Water Desalination System Driven by Heavy-Vehicle Traffic Through a Unilateral Speed-Bump Harvester
institutions: Doctorado en Ingeniería, Facultad de Ingeniería, Universidad del Magdalena, Carrera 32 No. 22-08, Santa Marta 470004, Colombia
Energy Department, Universidad de la Costa, Cl. 58 #55-66, Barranquilla 080002, Colombia
Civil Engineering Program, Faculty of Engineering, Universidad Militar Nueva Granada, Campus Cajicá, Cajicá 250247, Colombia
Facultad de Ingeniería, Universidad del Magdalena, Carrera 32 No. 22-08, Santa Marta 470004, Colombia
works.abstract: Traffic energy harvesting has been studied almost exclusively for electricity, and no transient model couples the full mechanical-to-hydraulic chain of a speed bump that pressurizes brackish water for reverse osmosis while treating the wheel–bump contact as a unilateral constraint. This work formulates such a model: half-car dynamics with pitch, a unilaterally constrained speed bump, four single-acting pistons with check-valve rectification, a hydropneumatic accumulator with adiabatic charge and isothermal discharge, and a solution-diffusion RO element with emergent recovery. The contact law transmits to the platform only the compressive tire load, the static axle load minus the dynamic extension, which is also the lift-off threshold; the tire spring of the vehicle model remains bilateral and the effect of that asymmetry is bounded. An event-driven Runge–Kutta scheme converges at first order; a nine-step study of the reference event shows every reported quantity within 0.7% of its limit; the model is verified but not experimentally validated. For a 10,500 kg vehicle at 30 km/h, the tires deliver 8.98 kJ and the accumulator stores 8.03 kJ (89.3%); the end stop takes 1.5%. The platform is driven by the static axle load and the lighter axle bounds the design. The event pumps 3.58 L and yields 1.21 L of permeate at 1.81 kWh/m3 and 788 mg/L from a 16.7 g/L feed. Across six commercial modules selectivity, not water permeability, sets product quality; a 1 km/h sweep without clipping shows weak speed sensitivity and a re-impact band at 14 to 20 km/h. The objective is to demonstrate by numerical modeling that the chain works and where it loses energy. At about one liter of non-potable water per vehicle the production is limited; competitiveness with conventional desalination has not been established, and the model includes no techno-economic assessment.

works.title: Removal of Endocrine-Disrupting Chemicals from Water Using Advanced Oxidation Processes (AOPs) and Ozonation
works.abstract: This study evaluates the nanofiltration (NF) and ozonation of the resulting concentrates for six target compounds: N,N-diethyl-m-toluamide (DEET), 3-(4-methylbenzylidene)camphor (4MBC), triclosan (TRC), carbamazepine (CBZ), estrone (E1), and estradiol (E2). The experiments were performed on surface water. The supplied endpoint data showed strongly compound-dependent membrane behavior. NF removal ranged from 33 to 75% for most detected compounds. Ozonation of the NF concentrate was highly effective for CBZ, TRC, 4MBC, E1, and E2 at both nominal doses, while DEET remained comparatively resistant. The nominal dose of ozone increased from 150 to 300 mg/L. The results demonstrate the potential of coupling dense-membrane separation with oxidative retentate treatment.

works.title: Membrany polimerowe w usuwaniu mikroplastiku z wód i ścieków – skuteczność, fouling i potencjalne uwalnianie cząstek
works.abstract: A review, with 54 refs., of the role and significance of polym. membranes in modern water and wastewater management. Membrane sepn. technols., with particular emphasis on microfiltration (MF), ultrafiltration (UF), nanofiltration (NF), reverse osmosis (RO), and membrane bioreactors (MBR) were discussed, noting their high efficiency in retaining microparticles and synthetic microfibers (ranging from 81.5 to 99.89%). Operational challenges, particularly membrane fouling, remain a significant barrier to the widespread industrial application of these technols. Fouling leads to increased filtration resistance, higher energy consumption, and the need for frequent chem. cleaning. Furthermore, attention was drawn to the environmental implications concerning the life cycle of polym. membranes; under intensive use, thermal and chem. aging, and disposal processes, these membranes can become a source of secondary microplastics released into the environment. In response to these limitations, current research focuses on material modifications designed to impart hydrophilic properties and fouling resistance to membrane surfaces, as well as on monitoring the secondary release of microplastics from the polym. components of membrane modules into the medium being treated.

works.title: Tailoring hydrophobic <scp>PDMS</scp> – <scp>PVDF</scp> membranes via solvent–polymer compatibility and additives for membrane distillation desalination
works.journal: The Canadian Journal of Chemical Engineering
institutions: Department of Chemical Engineering Malaviya National Institute of Technology Jaipur Jaipur India
Department of Chemical Engineering Sardar Vallabhbhai National Institute of Technology Surat Surat India
works.abstract: Abstract Membrane wetting and limited operational stability remain major challenges in membrane distillation, and both are strongly influenced by solvent selection and phase‐inversion behaviour. In this study, the polymer–solvent compatibility of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) was evaluated using Hansen solubility parameter (HSP) distance analysis to guide the fabrication of solution‐blended PDMS–PVDF membranes. Four solvents—NMP, DMF, DMSO, and THF—were investigated. The HSP results indicated that NMP and DMF are compatible with PVDF, while THF exhibited stronger affinity for PDMS. Accordingly, PVDF was dissolved in NMP and DMF, and PDMS in THF. Additives, including PEG‐400, H 3 PO 4 , and toluene, were incorporated. NMP‐based membranes demonstrated higher hydrophobicity, with the PEG‐400‐modified membrane exhibiting a water contact angle of 104.3°, compared to 83.9° for the DMF‐based system. Membrane porosity ranged from 51.42% to 57.8%. AFM analysis revealed maximum surface roughness (Ra = 5.554 nm; Sq = 7.389 nm) for the PEG‐400‐modified membrane. SEM, XRD, and FTIR analyses confirmed favourable morphology and structural characteristics. During VMD desalination of a 20,000 mg L −1 NaCl solution, the permeate flux decreased from 18.5 to 17.6 kg m −2 h −1 over 180 h, while salt rejection remained approximately 99.77%. The selected membrane exhibited an LEP of approximately 294.5 kPa and a maximum thermal efficiency of 93.70%. The integration of HSP‐guided solvent screening, controlled additive comparison, solution blending, and long‐term VMD validation distinguishes this work from conventional solvent‐screening studies.

works.title: Design and evaluation of a portable multifunctional nanofibrous membrane with photocatalytic activity for water purification: from in silico to in vitro
works.abstract: Access to clean, safe drinking water is a vital global priority, demanding rapid, reliable, and portable on-demand purification technologies for emergency response, field operations, and remote communities. In this study, a multifunctional portable membrane (designated as NFi) composed of electrospun nylon-6 functionalised with zinc oxide nanoparticles (N-6@ZnO) and polycaprolactone integrated with graphene oxide (PCL@GO) was engineered for high-performance water treatment. Molecular modeling-utilizing Density Functional Theory with dispersion corrections (DFT-D) and Monte Carlo (MC) adsorption locator simulations-elucidated the robust energetic affinity and favourable thermodynamic interactions governing the N-6@ZnO/PCL@GO hybrid architecture, evidenced by negative adsorption energies. Structurally, the electrospun fibrous network features mean pore dimensions of 627.3 nm (pristine N-6/PCL) to 793.0 nm (N-6@ZnO/PCL@GO), classifying the matrix geometrically within the microfiltration regime while providing interconnected mass-transfer channels. Under an operating pressure of 2 bar, the resulting N-6@ZnO/PCL@GO membrane demonstrated an outstanding pure water flux of 2,037 L·m−2·h−1 (pure water permeability of 1,019 L⋅m−2⋅h−1⋅bar−1), representing a ∼40% enhancement over the pristine N-6/PCL membrane (1,455 L⋅m−2⋅h−1⋅bar−1). Concurrently, the membrane demonstrated remarkable separation and degradation capabilities, achieving 99.2% rejection/photodegradation of methylene blue (MB) and total elimination (100% bactericidal efficacy) of both Gram-negative (Escherichia coli) and Gram-positive (Enterococcus) pathogens under visible/UV light irradiation via synergistic photocatalytic ROS generation and contact killing. These findings establish that combining nanofibrous electrospun scaffolding with photocatalytically active nano-inclusions yields an efficient, low-resistance, and highly portable platform for rapid water decontamination.

works.title: Membrane integrated bioprocessing of 1,3‐propanediol: biosynthesis, fouling, sustainable and techno‐economic perspectives
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
works.abstract: Microbial conversion of glucose or glycerol to 1,3‐propanediol (1,3‐PDO) is attractive, but recovery from dilute, protein, and salt‐rich broths often account for more than half of production cost. Membranes are widely proposed to ease this burden, yet the literature groups operations with very different tasks. This review organizes membrane operations by function (cell retention and clarification, desalting and impurity removal, water removal and concentration) and grades the evidence for each as obtained with real 1,3‐PDO broth with synthetic solutions or transferred from other applications. Only MF/UF clarification is well supported by broth data (96.95% 1,3‐PDO recovery with 96.30% cell removal on a 100 kDa membrane but flux falling by 69–92% within 5 min in dead end tests). Because 1,3‐PDO (76 Da) permeates UF and NF membranes, these cannot concentrate it, concentration by membrane distillation, pervaporation or reverse osmosis is far less well demonstrated. 1,3‐PDO specific fouling and cleaning evidence is limited to a few studies; most derives from wastewater systems. Order of magnitude analysis shows that water removal is dominated by latent heat (about 26 MJ kg −1 1,3‐PDO for single effect evaporation at 60 g L −1 ) and that titer matters as much as technology, so a generic 40% energy saving is unsupported. Published techno economic and life cycle studies do not resolve the membrane subsystem. Membranes are best used for clarification, desalting, and possibly preconcentration in hybrid trains ending with distillation or adsorption. Demonstrating their benefit requires long term pilot data on real broth and assessments that include the membrane subsystem. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).

works.title: Aquaporin biomonomer functionalized <scp>GUVs</scp> crosslinked cryogenic membrane for selective ammonia separation
institutions: Department of Chemistry Eskişehir Technical University, Faculty of Science Eskişehir Türkiye
BİONKİ Co. Ltd., Anadolu University Teknopark Eskişehir Türkiye
works.abstract: Abstract Giant unilamellar vesicles (GUVs) are a cornerstone of biomimetic membrane research, providing a versatile platform for studying membrane proteins, such as aquaporin, under conditions that closely resemble natural cellular environments. Integrating aquaporins into GUV membranes represents an emerging frontier in biomimetic tools that combine biological precision with synthetic flexibility and enhanced mechanical stability. These hybrid structures offer unprecedented opportunities to develop advanced technologies for artificial kidneys, water purification, and the removal of hazardous molecules such as ammonia. This study involved constructing micron‐sized GUVs with biomimetic permeability and incorporating highly selective aquaporin proteins. A specially designed functional monomer ensured stable localization of aquaporins (Aqp) on the GUV membrane, enhancing their positional stability. The Aqp@GUV system was evaluated in vitro for its artificial cell‐like structure, chemical selectivity, and ammonia permeability. The results show that this hybrid structure is a precise, selective, flexible, and mechanically stable biomimetic filtration system.

works.title: Atomic Layer Ordering of 2D van der Waals Ion Channels Enables Ultrathin and Highly Selective Membranes
works.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
institutions: Institute of Atomic and Molecular Sciences, Academia Sinica
works.abstract: Developing ultrathin, highly selective membranes that emulate biological ion channels is a primary goal of synthetic membrane technology. Although two-dimensional (2D) materials offer a promising platform for constructing subnanometer fluidic channels, simultaneously achieving high permeance and excellent selectivity in 2D ionic membranes remains a significant challenge. This bottleneck originates from the complexities involved in controlling the precise structural arrangement within nanosheet assemblies. In this work, we demonstrate that the atomic-layer ordering of 2D van der Waals (vdW) ion channels is a decisive factor in achieving ultrathin, highly selective membranes. By assembling 2D titania nanosheets with atomic layer-by-layer regularity, we fabricate atomic stacking membranes (ASMs) that achieve near-unity ion selectivity within an ultrathin (∼50 nm) framework. The structural regularity of these ASMs causes continuous overlap of the electrical double layer throughout the 2D ion channels, facilitating robust electrostatic regulation and maximizing selectivity. The result is further confirmed by transmission electron microscopy, grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations. Leveraging the “Lego-like” modular assembly advantage of ASMs, we demonstrate multifunctional heterostructural iontronic devices and gate-controlled iontronic transistors featuring on/off ratios up to 104. Furthermore, the well-ordered 2D ion channels within these ASMs enable high-performance osmotic energy harvesting. This solution-processable atomic-layer van der Waals assembly strategy for ultrathin and highly selective ASMs establishes a versatile platform for uniformly regulating 2D angstrom-scale ion transport, paving the way for advanced biomimetic iontronics and efficient energy conversion.

works.title: Process Integrated Comparative Assessment of Conventional and On-Purpose 1,3-Butadiene Production: Energy, Separation, and Decarbonization Perspectives
works.abstract: Abstract 1,3-Butadiene (1,3-BD) is one of the most commercially significant petrochemical monomers, underpinning the global synthetic rubber and plastics industries. Historically, it has been produced primarily as a byproduct of steam cracking of naphtha; however, the transition of global ethylene production toward lighter, shale gas-derived feedstocks has resulted in considerable strain in its sustainable availability (Samsudin, I. B.; et al.Chem. Asian J2020, 15, 24, 4199−4214.). This review provides a process-integrated comparative assessment of conventional and on-purpose 1,3-butadiene production technologies, evaluated through the lenses of energy consumption, separation performance, and decarbonization potential. The conventional C4 extraction route and its state-of-the-art NMP based separation technology are critically analyzed alongside a spectrum of on-purpose alternatives, including oxidative dehydrogenation (ODH) of n-butenes, direct dehydrogenation of n-butane, ethanol-to-butadiene (ETB) processes, butanediol dehydration routes, and emerging electrochemical pathways ( Brencio, C.; et al.Int. J. Hydrogen Energy2022, 47, 50, 21375−21390.,Teh, W. J.; et al.Nat. Catal.2024, 7, 12, 1382–1393.,Mantingh, J.; et al.Sep. Purif. Technol2021, 267, 118656.). Key findings indicate that while conventional steam cracking coupled with optimized extractive distillation remains the most energy-mature technology, its dependence on fossil feedstock and substantial greenhouse gas footprint makes it increasingly incompatible with net-zero industrial targets ( Cespi, D.; et al.Green Chem2016, 18, 6, 1625−1638.,Maga, D.; et al.Chem. Ing. Tech.2024, 96, 5, 688–697.). Among on-purpose routes, the biobased ETB one-step (Lebedev) process and 1,3-butanediol dehydration exhibit the most promising decarbonization profiles, despite current cost-competitiveness challenges relative to fossil-derived butadiene ( Camacho, C. E. C.; et al.J. Clean. Prod2022, 374, 133963.,Janssens, P.; et al.Ind. Eng. Chem. Res2025, 64, 45, 21571–21587.). Future process integration strategies, including heat pump-assisted distillation, dividing wall columns, membrane reactor technologies, and renewable energy coupling, are identified as essential levers for achieving technically and economically viable low-carbon butadiene supply chains. This review presents a unique cross-route analytical framework that simultaneously addresses energy demand, separation technology, C4 extraction solvent performance comparison, and life cycle carbon footprint across the full spectrum of 1,3-butadiene production routes from conventional steam cracking to biobased ethanol conversion, butanediol dehydration, furfural-derived pathways, natural gas integration, and the recently reported electrochemical route.

works.title: Suppressing Mg <sup>2+</sup> ‐Induced Failure of LATP Membranes for Lithium Separation Using a Low‐Barrier Graphite Interface
institutions: School of Metallurgy and Environment Central South University Changsha China
School of Energy and Power Engineering Changsha University of Science and Technology Changsha China
National Energy Metal Resources and New Materials Key Laboratory Changsha China
Institute of Process Engineering Chinese Academy of Sciences Beijing China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT High Mg/Li ratios and coexisting ions in salt‐lake brines limit the long‐term selectivity and structural stability of Li 1.3 Al 0.3 Ti 1.7 (PO 4 ) 3 (LATP) membranes. To address interfacial mass‐transfer resistance and Mg 2+ ‐induced performance decay, a graphite‐PVDF‐coated LATP membrane is constructed, enabling low‐resistance Li + transport while mitigating Mg 2+ interference. Under optimized conditions, the membrane increases Li + flux by ∼27% relative to pristine LATP, achieving a maximum Li–Mg separation factor of ∼6200 and a decreased water contact angle, indicating improved migration of hydrated Li + . Calculations show a lower Li + migration barrier in graphite than in LATP (0.27 vs. 0.68 eV), providing a low‐resistance pathway. Graphite also adsorbs Mg‐solvated clusters more strongly than Li‐solvated ones, reducing local Mg 2+ enrichment at the interface. DFT calculations suggest that Mg 2+ substitutes Ti/Al sites, lowering the Li + /H + exchange energy by 62.34 meV and reducing the Li/Mg migration‐barrier difference from 1.19 to 0.45 eV. HRTEM/SAED shows that the graphite‐PVDF layer mitigates lattice disorder, and TEM‐EDS reveals lower local Mg in the coated LATP after operation (0.23 vs. 0.49 wt.%). Long‐term tests show a ∼5‐fold longer service lifetime than the pristine membrane, providing insights into interfacial design for durable LATP‐based electrodialysis.

works.title: Membrane Adsorber-Based DLE: Enabling Fast Kinetics, Minimal Mn Loss, and Compatibility with Oilfield-Produced Water
works.abstract: Abstract In this study, we investigated the use of a Li-selective membrane synthesized with the incorporation of hydrogen manganese oxide (HMO) to simplify the extraction process. The HMO-loaded membranes (HMOM) displayed remarkable performance for direct lithium extraction (DLE). The major accomplishments of incorporating HMO within the polymeric substrate were 2-fold. First, fast kinetics were observed for HMOM; ∼90% capacity (15 mg/g) was attained in 5 min in the filtration mode, with a pseudo-second-order kinetic rate constant (k2) ∼20 times higher as compared to the batch test, owing to enhanced mass transfer within the regulated channels of the membrane. Second, incorporation of HMO in the poly(ether sulfone) matrix reduced the Mn loss by five times and showed only &lt;0.2% Mn loss per cycle during the DLE from produced water (PW) matrix. We showed that the acid concentration can be reduced by 10 times for Li recovery, which further displayed an additional 4-fold decrease in Mn loss but led to a ∼10% decline in Li recovery performance. HMOM also demonstrated competitive selectivity for Li against competing cations within PW, with a separation factor of ∼20–40. We demonstrate a multipass, multistage filtration process as a framework for sequential DLE, concentration, and purification from real PW.

works.title: Advanced Separation Technologies for Lithium Recovery from Brines: Performance, Economics and Sustainability
works.journal: The Sydney Journal of Interdisciplinary Engineering
works.abstract: Lithium carries the charge in the lithium-ion batteries used in electric vehicles (EVs), and demand for it is growing quickly. The International Energy Agency (IEA) expects about 23 million electric cars to be sold in 2026, and lithium demand could triple by 2040. Brines supply a large share of this lithium, as extraction from brine typically costs 30–50% less than mining hard rock. However, the conventional method of solar evaporation is slow, uses large amounts of water and only works on certain brines. Direct lithium extraction (DLE) offers an alternative. This review compares the three main DLE technologies, namely adsorption, membranes and electrochemical cells, along with the modelling and AI tools used to design them and the cost, sustainability and governance evidence that investors need. The Salar de Atacama in Chile is used as a case study. Most laboratory studies report high selectivity, but they use simplified brines, run for only a small number of cycles or hours, and stop at an enriched solution rather than a battery-grade product. Sorbents lose material, membranes foul, electrodes degrade, and reported energy figures often leave out pumping and regeneration. Evidently, selectivity or recovery alone cannot show which technology will be profitable. This review therefore recommends that investors compare technologies per kilogram of the same product, from pretreatment through to a specified purity. Before committing capital, investors should also ask for long trials on real brine, consistent reporting of water and energy use, and community participation. projectgroup13_458452_53577610_…

works.title: Pore-Wall Reconstruction Directs Monovalent-Ion Selectivity in Angstrom-Scale PIM Channels
institutions: East China University of Science and Technology , , ,
works.abstract: Abstract High-resolution discrimination among monovalent ions remains challenging because transport through confined polymer channels depends on subtle differences in hydration, partitioning, and ion–pore interactions. Here, stepwise pore-wall functional reconstruction of a common polymer of intrinsic microporosity scaffold directs ion transport toward complementary monovalent-cation- and monovalent-anion-selective functions. The rigid, contorted PIM backbone provides a pre-existing subnanometer free-volume network, allowing pore-wall functionality to regulate confined-water organization, pore accessibility, and local ion–polymer interactions within a common transport scaffold. Starting from PIM-1, amine-, amidoxime-, and guanidinium-functionalized derivatives were prepared to regulate channel polarity, hydrogen-bonding capability, local charge, and accessible free volume while preserving the rigid microporous framework. AO-PIM-1 combines interconnected hydration pathways with angstrom-scale confinement, achieving electrodialysis selectivities of 395.7 for K+/Mg2+ and 5.8 for K+/Li+ under optimized conditions. PIM-G instead forms positively charged, spatially restricted guanidinium-lined channels, yielding Cl–/SO42– and Cl–/F– selectivities of 60.6 and 6.9, respectively. Experiments and molecular simulations show that these contrasting behaviors arise from the cooperative regulation of confined-water organization, pore accessibility, and local ion–pore interactions, establishing pore-wall reconstruction as a molecular design route for high-resolution ion separation.

works.title: Floating or Sinking Carbon Dioxide Clathrate Hydrate in Brines: Density Determination and Relevance to Seawater Desalination
works.abstract: Abstract An experimental investigation was carried out to determine whether carbon dioxide clathrate hydrate, formed by reacting brines of various concentrations with carbon dioxide gas, floats or sinks in the remaining unreacted brine. This study aims to advance clathrate hydrate-based seawater desalination and/or salt production. The carbon dioxide clathrate hydrate formed in the reactors is recovered together with the unreacted seawater as slurry and then sent to the solid–liquid separation process. Understanding whether the hydrate floats or sinks is essential for the design and operation of the process. In this study, floating or sinking was determined by visual inspection when the system reached three-phase equilibrium among sodium chloride aqueous solution, carbon dioxide clathrate hydrate, and carbon dioxide gas. The equilibrium sodium chloride mass fraction in the brine ranged from 0.095 to 0.150. At higher mass fraction, the carbon dioxide clathrate hydrate floated in the aqueous solution. The critical mass fraction, defined as the average of the two mass fractions bounding the transition from sinking to floating, increased with pressure and was 0.109 ± 0.011 at approximately 1 MPa and 0.118 ± 0.007 at approximately 2 MPa. The corresponding equilibrium temperatures were approximately 266 and 272 K, respectively. Because sinking and floating correspond to opposite relative density orderings of the clathrate hydrate and the aqueous solution, the density of clathrate hydrate was determined from the density of aqueous solution at the corresponding intermediate condition to be 1092 ± 9 kg/m3 at about 1 MPa and 1105 ± 7 kg/m3 at about 2 MPa, suggesting that the hydrate density increases with increasing pressure. These density data were compared with values reported in previous studies based on physical characterization. Finally, the relevance of these findings to seawater desalination technology was discussed.

works.title: Techno-Economic and Performance Assessment of Battery versus Green Hydrogen Storage Systems for Large-Scale Grid Decarbonization
works.journal: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science and Technology
works.abstract: With an energy evolution taking hold, net-zero ambitions rapidly spread from the household to the organization to the grid.This paper conducts a systematic techno-economic and performance comparison of battery energy storage systems (BESS, specifically Lithium Iron Phosphate [〖"LiFePO" 〗_4 / LFP] and Vanadium Redox Flow Batteries [VRFB]) versus green hydrogen energy storage systems (GHESS, utilizing polymer electrolyte membrane [PEM] electrolyzers, geological cavern/compressed storage, and PEM/combined cycle fuel conversion) across discharge durations of 4 to 120 hours.A techno-economic assessment evaluates Levelized Cost of Storage (LCOS), Round-Trip Efficiency (RTE), footprint, cyclic degradation, and capital scaling metrics.The study found that while BESS achieves higher RTE (72.0% to 84.0%) and clear cost leadership below 8 hours, its capital cost barrier at higher durations scales steeply due to linear cell-stack addition.In contrast, the GHESS architecture decouples power capacity from energy capacity, achieving marginal capacity costs below $3/"kWh" (in geological salt caverns) and establishing economic crossover dominance from 14 to 16 hours of continuous discharge onward.A multi-objective hybrid architecture is modeled, demonstrating that pairing BESS for intra-day balancing with GHESS for synoptic, multi-day reserves minimizes total system curtailment and yields an optimized levelized cost profile for zero-emission bulk power utilities.

works.title: Encapsulating Metal–Organic Cluster in Metal–Organic Framework Film for Tandem Amplifying Third‐Order Nonlinear Optics
institutions: State Key Laboratory of Structural Chemistry Fujian Institute of Research on the Structure of Matter Chinese Academy of Sciences Fuzhou Fujian China
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences Beijing China
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and metal–organic clusters (MOCs) are promising platforms for third‐order nonlinear optics (NLO) because their inorganic–organic components enable designable structures and tunable photo/electronic properties. However, integrating MOFs and MOCs for tandem third‐order NLO remains unexplored. Here, we combine MOF and MOC for third‐order NLO by encapsulating MOC in a porous MOF film. A [001]‐oriented conductive MOF Ni‐HHTP film (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexahydroxytriphenylene) is prepared by liquid‐phase heating drop‐coating and shows excellent electro‐regulated third‐order NLO. Furthermore, iron‐based MOC (FeOC) is encapsulated into the ordered nanochannels of Ni‐HHTP film (Ni‐HHTP@FeOC) using an immersion strategy. The results show that the encapsulation of FeOC in the Ni‐HHTP film can enhance charge transfer and improve excited‐state absorption, with the nonlinear absorption coefficient ( β ) increasing from 4.9 × 10 −6 to 9.7 × 10 −6 m/W after loading. An applied electric field further modulates carrier concentration and excited‐state lifetime, enabling dynamic adjustment of the third‐order NLO response; β increased to 19.6 × 10 −6 m/W for Ni‐HHTP@FeOC‐2 V. This work is the first to combine MOF and MOC materials for high third‐order NLO performance and provides a synergistic strategy for regulating third‐order NLO performance through tandem encapsulation and electronic stimulation, offering new design concepts for adaptive optoelectronic devices.

works.title: Constructing Dynamic Interfacial Hydration Network Channel for Efficient Co‑Transport of OH − and H 2 in Water‑Electrolysis Cathodes
works.abstract: Efficient mass transport at the electrode–electrolyte interface of anion‐exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEM‐WE) is fundamentally constrained by antagonistic hydration requirements. Drawing inspiration from biological channels that mediate hydrophilic yet non‐retentive transport, we designed a series of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with tunable sulfone densities as synthetic nanochannels. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations revealed that the sulfone moiety (O═S═O) established weak, labile hydrogen bonds with water, engendering a highly dynamic hydrogen‐bonding network. This unique hydration environment established a surface‐wetting yet bulk‐open state within the COF nanochannels, wherein a dynamic interfacial hydration network channel was maintained within the pores for efficient OH − conduction, while the bulk pore volume remained non‐flooded for unobstructed H 2 evacuation. When incorporated into the cathode catalyst layer, the sulfone‐rich 2S‐COF delivers a current density of 10.30 A cm −2 at 2.0 V under industrially relevant conditions (1 M KOH, 80°C), representing a 48% enhancement over the COF‐free electrode. This work establishes a bio‐inspired strategy for molecular‐level control of interfacial hydration, providing a generalizable platform for designing high‐performance electrochemical interfaces that require concurrent ion and gas management.

The results show that the encapsulation of FeOC in the Ni‐HHTP film can enhance charge transfer and improve excited‐state absorption, with the nonlinear absorption coefficient ( β ) increasing from 4.9 × 10 −6 to 9.7 × 10 −6 m/W after loading. An applied electric field further modulates carrier concentration and excited‐state lifetime, enabling dynamic adjustment of the third‐order NLO response; β increased to 19.6 × 10 −6 m/W for Ni‐HHTP@FeOC‐2 V. This work is the first to combine MOF and MOC materials for high third‐order NLO performance and provides a synergistic strategy for regulating third‐order NLO performance through tandem encapsulation and electronic stimulation, offering new design concepts for adaptive optoelectronic devices.

works.title: Advancements in Solar Drying Technology: Enhancing Food Preservation and Solar Power Systems for Sustainable Solutions
institutions: Vignan's Foundation for Science, Technology & Research
works.abstract: Global food insecurity and escalating postharvest losses, which affect nearly one‐third of total food production, necessitate sustainable preservation technologies aligned with the Food and Agriculture Organization targets and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Solar drying has emerged as an energy‐efficient and environmentally benign alternative to conventional fossil‐fuel‐based dehydration methods. This review critically examines advancements in direct, indirect, and hybrid solar drying systems, evaluating their design configurations, thermal performance, operational parameters, and product quality outcomes. Comparative assessments indicate that hybrid systems integrating auxiliary heating (biomass, electric, or heat pumps) enhance drying reliability under fluctuating climatic conditions while improving overall thermo‐economic efficiency. The study further explores advanced performance‐enhancement strategies, including jet‐impingement air heaters, thermal energy storage (sensible, latent, and thermochemical systems), desiccant‐assisted dehumidification, nanofluid‐based heat‐transfer augmentation, and solar thermal selective coatings. Integration of phase change materials and composite desiccants significantly improves moisture removal rates, energy efficiency, and off‐sunshine operability. Emerging nanofluid and surface‐modification technologies demonstrate notable improvements in collector efficiency and heat‐transfer coefficients. The review identifies current technical limitations, economic considerations, and scalability challenges while outlining future research directions for high‐efficiency, sustainable solar drying systems applicable to agricultural and industrial sectors.

works.title: Removal of copper and lead ions by red mud-metakaolin-based geopolymer microspheres: Insights into efficient preparation and adsorption mechanisms
works.abstract: This study used red mud and metakaolin as the main raw materials, with sodium silicate as the alkali activator. Red mud-metakaolin-based geopolymer microspheres (RM-MGMs) with good sphericity and high mechanical strength were prepared via the dispersion-suspension-solidification method. By investigating the adsorption performance of RM-MGMs calcined at different temperatures for Cu2+ and Pb2+, the uncalcined RM-MGMs exhibit excellent heavy metal cation adsorption due to their abundant surface hydroxyl groups and high ion exchange capacity. The optimal adsorption conditions for Cu2+/Pb2+ were adsorbent dosages of 1.5/0.3 g L−1 and pH of 5.3–5.6/5.0. Cu2+ adsorption reached equilibrium at 960 min. Pb2+ showed a faster adsorption rate due to its smaller hydrated ionic radius and reached equilibrium at 60 min. Kinetic results indicated that the pseudo-second-order model better described the adsorption process of RM-MGMs for Cu2+/Pb2+. Adsorption isotherm models showed that increasing temperature favored the adsorption of Cu2+/Pb2+ by RM-MGMs. At 318 K, the adsorption capacities of RM-MGMs for Cu2+/Pb2+ reach 0.87/1.43 mmol g−1, respectively. In competitive experiments, the removal rates of Cu2+/Pb2+ by RM-MGMs both exceed 80%. RM-MGMs achieve adsorption of Cu2+/Pb2+ through synergistic mechanisms including ion exchange, electrostatic attraction, and complexation.
